convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom() calls to the 'SilverTrend' custom indicator which is not a built-in MT5 indicator. The custom indicator's internal logic is not accessible from the EA source alone, requiring separate analysis or reimplementation of the SilverTrend indicator in Python.

other_exits: Opposite SilverTrend signal closes existing position before opening new one in reverse direction

custom_logic_notes: The EA relies entirely on the SilverTrend custom indicator for signal generation. It reads two buffers from iCustom: buffer 0 for buy signals (non-zero = signal active) and buffer 1 for sell signals (non-zero = signal active). When an opposite signal appears, the existing position is closed first (signal_reversal_close). The new bar check prevents multiple entries within the same bar. SL and TP default to 0 meaning no protective stops are placed - the EA relies solely on signal reversal for exits, making it a signal-reversal-only system.
external_dependencies: SilverTrend.ex5 (custom indicator, must be available in Indicators directory)
python_conversion_notes: The SilverTrend indicator logic must be reverse-engineered or obtained separately. The indicator typically implements a noise-filtering algorithm using weighted moving averages and ATR-like volatility measure. The RISK parameter controls sensitivity (lower = more signals, higher = fewer but stronger signals). CountBars is the lookback window. Without the indicator source, the Python conversion will need the .mq5 source of SilverTrend to replicate the buffer calculations. The EA shell itself is simple: new bar detection, position check, signal read, close opposite, open new. No digit adjustment is performed on SL/TP since both are 0.
